note: ADDENDUM to mapping-2026-11-03.json for the one response added by the 2026-11-14 export (survey-r15). tools/survey_to_claims.py merges every mapping-<date>.json in date order, so the 14-response mapping stays in force unchanged. Keyed by anonymous respondent id and the raw name as typed; nothing here identifies a respondent. Every decision below is DRAFTED BY THE CODING AGENT 2026-11-13 AND AWAITS KAY'S APPROVAL (see reports/survey-delta-2026-11-14.md, 'Decisions for review').

respondent_public.note: public-record generalisation. The respondent ticked two roles; that combination occurs once in the 15 responses and would narrow a small local professional community to very few people, so the tracked record keeps one role. baseline_confidence is computed from the answers as given (the value is the same either way: 0.8, the cap).

survey-r15.privacy_note: one further self-reported role withheld from the public record (unique combination in the sample; re-identification risk)

restored_text.note: one d2 note on an out-of-DB candidate from the 14-response set lost its spaces (form bug, M21); restored here so the candidate evidence queue is readable. raw_export_text is kept on the queue entry.

value.selection_reason: leaf appearance — how the heart-shaped leaves are held on the stem

survey-r15|Cercidiphyllum japonicum.mapping_note: a designer's personal aesthetic reason for choosing the plant (follows the survey-r07 precedent for aesthetic reasons). NOT a verified leaf trait, NOT a form/habit value, and NOT evidence for any spatial function (Screen, opacity). Stored as selection_reason, L0, not citable.

candidates_not_in_db.note: raw names typed by survey-r15 that resolve to no plant in the database. Names are kept exactly as typed. taxon_review 'pending' = the identity below is a provisional reading used only so the name resolves to a stable id; it is not an accepted taxon decision. 'Stewartia pseudocamellia' needs no entry: it already resolves to the existing out-of-DB candidate stewartia-pseudocamellia through that entry's scientific name (second mention, not a new entity).

entries.note: typed as A. alnifolia 'Autumn Brilliance'. The cultivar name 'Autumn Brilliance' is usually listed under Amelanchier × grandiflora, while A. alnifolia is the native saskatoon — the respondent may mean either. Species NOT decided; check before canonicalising.
respondent named the cultivar 'Gracillimus'; species-level id following the lavandula-angustifolia precedent. Cultivar identity not independently checked.
respondent's spelling 'sanguinem'; read as Ribes sanguineum (red-flowering currant) — a probable reading, not a confirmed identification.

candidate_review.note: researcher notes attached to entries of data/survey/candidate_evidence.json (keyed by queue entry id).

cand:survey-r15:d2.review_note: experience-based practitioner note (basis: mixed — the respondent ticked 'A combination of these'; own design use is stated in the text). Reports lodging of large plants after heavy rain and a need for division every few years. No location, site conditions, plant age or maintenance regime recorded. An attributed anecdote — not a general characteristic of the cultivar.
